note: The artifact the raft-rs-wasm backend loads, how it was built, and the raft-rs 0.7 sources the host contract is cited against. Integrity is required; reproducibility is measured and reported as found.

reproducibility.method: the recorded build command run twice on one machine with `cargo clean` between them (attempts 1 and 2, one source); attempt 3 is the checked-in artifact after the fork fixes and is a DIFFERENT source, so it is not part of the reproducibility comparison

builds.note: after the three fork fixes; not comparable to the earlier attempts, which were a different source

reproducibility.observation: the generated JavaScript glue is byte-identical across both builds; the .wasm is not. Reported as measured; byte-for-byte reproducibility is not a requirement of this quest.
reproducibility.note: attempts 1-3 measured the reproducibility of ONE source; attempt 4 is a different source (the fork fixes) and is the checked-in artifact. The reproducibility verdict below refers to attempts 1 and 2.

seededBuild.method: the recorded build command run twice with cargo clean between them on the patched source (attempts 5 and 6); attempt 6 is the checked-in artifact
seededBuild.observation: the glue is byte-identical to every earlier build (no export was added: the seed crosses inside the existing create_node options). The two .wasm builds have the same size and differ in 36 bytes, all inside the import section: wasm-bindgen emitted its __wbindgen_cast_* placeholder imports in a different order. Reported as measured, as before.

forkFixes.fix: with_node takes the node out of the handle table for the duration of the call
forkFixes.why: a raft-rs fatal! inside the closure left the NODES RefCell borrowed for ever (panic=abort on wasm32, so no unwinding and no catch_unwind); every later call on EVERY handle then trapped "RefCell already borrowed", including create_node and free. Measured before and after.

forkFixes.fix: decode_conf_change_entry returns an error on undecodable base64
forkFixes.why: upstream unwrap_or_default() turned corrupt data into an EMPTY change list, which is a valid request to leave a joint configuration

forkFixes.fix: pending_conf_index crosses as a decimal string
forkFixes.why: it was the one u64 crossing as a JS number

forkFixes.fix: every recoverable binding refusal crosses as a tagged object
forkFixes.why: the private invocation owner must distinguish CORE_REFUSED from a WASM trap by construction, without inspecting a generic JavaScript exception class or message

forkFixes.fix: create_node takes an optional electionSeed (decimal u64) and passes it to the patched raft Config::election_timeout_seed
forkFixes.why: owner decision O2: a host-supplied seed makes every randomized election timeout of a node a function of (seed, node id) and keeps a seeded core off the platform entropy source; an absent seed is the previous behaviour

vendoredAt: vendor/raft-rs-wasm — generated and vendored infrastructure for the experimental raft-rs-wasm backend the provider seam selects. It lives outside src/ because wasm-pack output is nobody's source: keeping it out of the source tree is what lets every repository checker stay on its own default walk with no exclusion for it. Moved here from the exhausted raft-backend-evaluation test tree (tag raft-backend-evaluation/round-3-rejected-tree); the .wasm and the glue are byte-identical to the tagged tree, which the two digests above prove.

citationSources.note: The raft-rs 0.7.0 sources the host contract cites, vendored so a citation resolves without a cargo registry. The chain is: the crates.io checksum recorded as raftCrateChecksum is the sha256 of the published .crate tarball; these files were extracted from that tarball and their own digests recorded here.

raftCratePatch.note: owner decision O2: the artifact is compiled from raft 0.7.0 as published (raftCrateChecksum) with ONE patch, applied through [patch.crates-io] in Cargo.toml to the crate vendored under raft-0.7.0/: Config::election_timeout_seed. None (the default) keeps upstream reset_randomized_election_timeout unchanged (rand::thread_rng, seeded from getrandom js -> crypto.getRandomValues); Some(seed) draws every randomized election timeout from a SplitMix64 stream owned by the node and started from splitmix64(seed ^ splitmix64(id)). Every other vendored file is byte-identical to the file of the same path in the crates.io tarball; vendoredFiles records the digest of every file under raft-0.7.0/ as checked in.

raftCrateSource: vendored raft-0.7.0/ with the raftCratePatch (Cargo.lock records it as a path dependency, so it carries no registry checksum)
